doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Flip Benson, Grand Rapids and the Army
title: Members of Flip's band and their Blue Devils roots
summary: Ware describes the older musicians, Skeets Washley, Charles Copeland and others, who came out of the southwestern territory bands.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Did you have a set kind of show that you played with Flip's band?
Or did you play the drums in Flip's ...

No, I didn't play the drums in Flip's band. Every night, we had a little show we put on -- only if it was necessary though, if they called for it. But other than that, we just played dance music. And we'd do our little flash thing.
Flip and his band -- now these guys were older dudes and the younger cat beside me was Skeets -- he was the tenor player. Skeets was -- he had to be about 30 something, and I was 15.

Skeets Washley was his name. He was out of Hannibal, Missouri. And Flip -- and Charles, our alto player, was out of Texas; his drummer was out of Kansas City, George Smith; Mitch Franklin was out from the southwest somewhere out there; he's still living, and Flip -- now, I can't remember exactly where Flip was from -- but they all come out of that Blue Devil's Band, you see; they worked -- and Flip told me he had worked with Walter Page Blue Devil's big band man, and they were on good
terms with Nat Towles -- those kind of bands out in the southwest, and they'd been traveling for years. You know, before I joined them.
Like I said, this was an education for me.
